text:
sam: customer acme-inc reported p99 jump ~12s starting 10:14 UTC after the coalescer rollout. they see timeouts and retries piling up. stack: hosted-inference-prod, model: rw-large-v2, route: /v1/generate

nina: seeing same on infra dashboards — p95 up ~300ms, p99 up to 12s on a subset of nodes (az-eu-west-2b). spike aligns with continuous-coalesce v2 enable.

liam: any config diff? I remember we changed the coalescer backoff algorithm + enabled adaptive-queue-sampling.

jess: confirmed: rollout at 10:12 UTC. config snippet used: ```yaml
continuous_coalesce:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 30
  adaptive_backoff: true
  min_wait_ms: 0
```

sam: interesting — min_wait_ms=0 might allow very small requests to repeatedly loop and cause queue thrash. logs show repeated enqueue/dequeue for same request id. snippet from debug logs: ```
[10:14:23.112] INFO coalesce: enqueue req=abc123 size=1
[10:14:23.142] INFO coalesce: dequeue req=abc123 batched=false wait_elapsed=29ms
[10:14:23.143] INFO coalesce: enqueue req=abc123 size=1
[10:14:23.172] WARN coalesce: late-dequeue req=abc123 total_wait=60ms
```

nina: that looks like oscillation where very small payloads wake the batcher but never reach max_batch_size, then backoff resets and repeats. results in extra scheduling overhead and KV cache churn -> increased token generation latency.

liam: repro locally with a synthetic stream? I can spin up a canary pool and replay small prompt traffic.

jess: doing a quick mitigation: rollback adaptive_backoff to false and set min_wait_ms to 4ms for canary. patch: ```diff
-  adaptive_backoff: true
-  min_wait_ms: 0
+  adaptive_backoff: false
+  min_wait_ms: 4
```

ops-bot: deploy-started canary coalesce-config -> pool: canary-eu-w2b, user: jess

sam: nice. while canary runs, let's gather metrics: coalesce.loop_count, coalesce.enqueue_rate, cpu_sys, p99_latency_per_node. Query (promql-ish): `rate(coalesce_enqueue_total[1m]) by (node)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, node))`

nina: canary results after 3 minutes: enqueue_rate stabilized down 45%, loop_count dropped, p99 on canary nodes fell from ~11.8s -> 320ms.

liam: looks good. what's the recommended global action? full rollback of adaptive_backoff or tune defaults?

jess: recommend merging patch to default config but with a gradual rollout and a safety guard: if coalesce.enqueue_rate increases by >20% or p99 delta > 200ms in any az, auto-rollout-stop. Also add a short-circuit for tiny payloads (<32 tokens) to prefer immediate small batches with fixed short timeout.

sam: agree. add a migration note to telemetry team to add a metric `tiny_payload_throttle_count` so we can track policy hits.

ops-bot: deploy-succeeded canary coalesce-config -> pool: canary-eu-w2b

nina: after gradual rollout to 50% capacity, cluster-wide p99 improved vs prior spike. we should backfill alert thresholds: lower the burst alarm for coalesce.loop_count on prod for next 24h.

liam: I'll prepare a postmortem blameless doc with root cause: aggressive adaptive_backoff + min_wait=0 caused coalescer oscillation for solo/tiny requests -> scheduling overhead and cache pressure -> p99 tail spike. include repro steps and the quick mitigation.

jess: also added an e2e test in the coalescer CI that simulates a stream of single-token requests at rps=1000 for 60s and checks p99 < 1s under default config.

sam: outstanding. action items: [liam] write postmortem, [jess] PR default config + safety guard, [nina] temp alert tuning, [sam] notify support and acme-inc that we've rolled mitigations and will monitor.

support note (sam): "We've deployed a configuration rollback and mitigations targeted at coalescer oscillation; p99 has returned to baseline for canary and partial rollout. We'll continue monitoring and follow up with a summary and next steps." :thumbsup:
